title: The three main chords
summary: I, IV and V: home, away and the pull back home.

steps.title: Primary chord
steps.body:
The I, IV and V chords are the three **primary chords** of a key. They are all major, and between them they hold every note of the scale. In C major they are C, F and G.

**Why it matters:** Thousands of songs use only these three chords. "Three chords and the truth" is a saying for a reason.

steps.title: Dominant
steps.body:
The V chord is called the **dominant**. It pulls strongly back to I. In C major the dominant is G.

**Why it matters:** Songs build tension on V and release it on I. Hearing that pull lets you guess where a song is going next.

steps.title: Subdominant
steps.body:
The IV chord is the **subdominant**. It moves away from home more gently. In C major it is F.

**Why it matters:** When a band says "go to the four", they mean the subdominant. It is the usual first step away from I.

steps.title: I, IV and V in G major
steps.body: G, C and D: the three primary chords of G major.

items.prompt: In G major, play the IV chord.
In G major, play the V chord.

steps.title: Home, away, back
steps.body: Play C, then F, then G, then C. Feel I as home, IV as stepping out, V as wanting to come back.

items.prompt: In G major, which chord is the V?
In F major, which chord is the IV?
